title: Choose the visual world: projector view
question: The roll assigned The Rulebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Rulebook
options.lineage: modern board-game rulebooks and their card decks
options.thesis: The bot's turn written out as a rulebook's numbered steps, played on a mat above.
options.viewport: Play mat on top: two cute tokens, each with a card stand (face-down = chosen). Below: 'The bot's turn' with steps 1 Predict, 2 Score, 3 Choose as collapsed numbered bars; extra panels as index tabs.
options.risk: Can tip into toy-box clutter if the cards and tokens compete with the matrices.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not a hue: a chosen player shows a face-down card, an opened step gets a check stamp, the step you stopped on gets a flag.
The collapsed step stack shows exactly how many steps remain; structure is the only ornament besides the two tokens.
Numbers are the material: every numeral tabular at one weight, no grey text anywhere on the projector.
One alarm colour, used only for the reveal moment and the 'differs from countering' flag.

options.label: The Cutaway
options.thesis: Click the robot's head and it opens like a cutaway diagram, each part labelled with its step.
options.viewport: Large cute robot right, its open head showing three labelled parts; leader lines run to collapsed callout boxes for Predict, Score, Choose; the human token and result banner on the left.
options.risk: The most literal reading of 'open its brain'; leader lines crowd once a 9×9 grid opens.

options.label: Sixteen-Colour Visual Novel
options.thesis: The match as a visual-novel scene: the bot's portrait on the right, its thinking in the docked text window.
materials: bitmap type on a cell grid
options.viewport: Full-height cute bot portrait right, human portrait chip left, a beveled window docked low listing the three steps as menu rows that invert when opened.
options.case: Fuses well: cute portraits and a dialogue window carry the 'brain unfurls' idea; holds audience identification, loses clarity under lights-on projection.
options.risk: Dark dithered ground washes out with the lights on; bitmap matrices strain at distance.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Steps strung as frames on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: Orange rail across black, steps as frames.
options.case: Loses both: black ground fails lights-on, film editing is foreign to the audience.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Exposed Binding
options.thesis: Sections bound with the structure showing.
options.viewport: A spine of stitches, each step a section.
options.case: Loses both: calm craft tone fights a live game; stitches add nothing to the maths.
options.kept: The structure shows how many steps remain.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white numeric fields.
options.viewport: Data columns with one inverted focus column.
options.case: Loses both: no room for cute, strobing hurts a talk; strong numerics alone don't carry the game.
options.risk: Cold, and strobe is unsafe in a classroom.
options.kept: Numbers as the material, no grey.

options.label: Calavera Broadside
options.thesis: Skeletons act out each round above dense verse.
options.viewport: Image band of skeletons, two verse columns below.
options.case: Loses both: skeletons aren't cute, two dense columns can't hold matrices.
options.risk: Tone mismatch for a class demo.
options.kept: One alarm colour, saved for the moment that matters.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Blocks of weather cut and stacked.
options.viewport: Stacked cloud blocks with blue voids between.
options.case: Loses both: no link to RPS or the maths; volumetrics cost the frame rate.
options.kept: Deep gaps between strata: stage and thinking get a clear band between them.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean interactive-lesson app: white cards, one indigo accent, rounded chips.
canonCard.viewport: Score header with two avatars, an accordion of three step cards below, a tab bar for extra panels.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every learning app; nothing ties it to this game.
